text:
We can confirm the Tamsin Reservoir repair came in at 48 million, according to the project ledger we reviewed this week. The three-year overhaul on the east embankment finished in late October after crews replaced 2.4 kilometers of cracked liner, reworked the spillway gates, and stabilized the access causeway. Our notes show the final payment cleared after the last pressure tests passed on 18 October. The repair team said contingency costs stayed below forecast because the silt removal phase finished early and the membrane shipment arrived on time.

- Total repair cost: 48 million
- Work completed: late October
- Main scope: liner replacement, spillway gate rework, embankment stabilization
- Final testing passed: 18 October
